;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian civil war]], [[Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)]]
**A [[Syrian Air Force]] helicopter is [[List of aviation shootdowns and accidents during the Syrian Civil War|shot down]] by a [[surface-to-air missile]] over the [[Aleppo Governorate|Aleppo]] countryside, killing both pilots. It is the second Syrian helicopter to be shot down this week by [[Turkey|Turkish]]-backed forces. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/syrian-rebels-shoot-down-second-government-helicopter-one-week (''Middle East Eye'')] [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-02/14/c_138784396.htm (Xinhuanet)]
*Remains of 6,032 people are found with thousands of bullets in six [[mass grave]]s in [[Karuzi Province]], [[Burundi]], the largest find yet of an excavation project into atrocities of the [[Burundian Civil War]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-burundi-graves/over-6000-bodies-found-in-burundis-mass-graves-idUSKBN2090GP?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Ntumbo attack]]
**At least 22 people are killed in an attack on a village in [[Northwest Region (Cameroon)|Northwest Region]], [[Cameroon]]. [https://bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-51526358 (BBC News)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Nepalese people|Nepalese]] [[Sherpa people|Sherpas]] condemn the [[Government of Nepal|Nepalese government]]'s plan to use the [[Nepalese Army|army]] to clear rubbish from the top of [[Mount Everest]] and five other [[Himalayas|Himalayan]] peaks, saying only experienced Sherpas can reach those places. An army spokesman says the army will be able to reach all those summits. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-51501086 (BBC News)]

;Business and economy
*[[Facebook]] and [[Instagram]] amend their advertising policies so that politicians are allowed to use [[Influencer marketing|influencers to promote their campaigns]], in response to U.S. presidential candidate [[Michael Bloomberg]] using them to advertise [[Michael Bloomberg 2020 presidential campaign|his candidacy]] without being subjected to both sites' regulations on political ads. [https://www.politico.com/news/2020/02/14/bloomberg-meme-changes-facebook-instagram-115333 (''Politico'')] [https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2020/feb/14/facebook-reverses-political-ads-rule-bloomberg-finds-loophole (''The Guardian'')] 
*Twenty-one [[U.S. state]]s reject a {{USD|18}}{{nbsp}}billion settlement offer by pharmaceutical manufacturers, such as [[McKesson Corporation]] and [[Johnson & Johnson]], for their role in the [[Opioid epidemic in the United States|opioid crisis]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/ajimpact/states-reject-opioid-makers-18bn-settlement-offer-200214234135829.html (Al Jazeera)]
*The [[Federal Aviation Administration|U.S. Federal Aviation Administration  ]] allows [[List of airlines of the United States|U.S. airlines]] to resume flight paths over much of the [[Persian Gulf]] and the [[Gulf of Oman]], after suspending it last month due to escalating military tensions with [[Iran]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-gulf-aviation/u-s-relaxes-restrictions-on-u-s-civilian-flights-over-gulf-idUSKBN2090QN?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt]]
***The first case of coronavirus infection in the [[Africa]]n continent is reported in [[Egypt]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/egypt-confirms-coronavirus-case-africa-200214190840134.html (Al Jazeera)]

;International relations
*[[Belarus–Russia relations]]
**[[Belarus]] threatens to take oil from the [[Druzhba pipeline]] which carries [[Russia]]n oil to central [[Europe]] across its territory, if Russia does not supply it with the required volumes of [[crude oil]]. [[Petroleum industry in Russia|Russian oil supplies]] to Belarus have not been agreed for 2020 and shipments have dwindled to 500,000 tonnes, down from a planned 2 million tonnes. [https://www.reuters.com/article/belarus-oil-lukashenko/update-1-belarus-threatens-to-take-oil-from-russian-transit-pipeline-belta-idUSL8N2AE4SW (Reuters)]
**[[President of Belarus|Belarusian President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] says Moscow hinted at an energy supply deal in exchange for Belarus merging with Russia, which caused talks to collapse. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-belarus-oil-russia-lukashenko/russia-hints-at-belarus-joining-it-in-a-unified-state-in-exchange-for-oil-deal-lukashenko-idUSKBN20815V (Reuters)] [https://www.nytimes.com/aponline/2020/02/14/world/europe/ap-eu-russia-belarus.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Sri Lanka–United States relations]]
**The [[United States Department of State|U.S. State Department]] sanctions [[Sri Lanka]]n [[Commander of the Army (Sri Lanka)|Army Commander]] [[Shavendra Silva]] for alleged [[Alleged war crimes during the final stages of the Sri Lankan Civil War|human rights violations]] during the [[Eelam War IV#The conclusion of the war|final phase]] of the [[Sri Lankan Civil War]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-sri-lanka/u-s-blacklists-sri-lankan-army-commander-cites-killings-abuses-idUSKBN2081UR?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Kosovo–Serbia relations]]
**[[President of Kosovo|Kosovar President]] [[Hashim Thaçi]] and [[President of Serbia|Serbian President]] [[Aleksandar Vučić]] agree to connect the capitals of their respective countries by rail and roads, in a deal brokered by the [[United States]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/milestone-kosovo-serbia-sign-rail-road-deals-200215021536359.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Law and crime
*[[Terrorism in Germany]]
**Twelve men are arrested in [[Germany]] for attempting to start a [[Far-right politics in Germany (1945–present)|far-right organization]] aimed at carrying out attacks against politicians, [[asylum seeker]]s, and [[Islam in Germany|Muslims]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/suspects-germany-planned-attack-muslims-refugees-200214141816203.html (Al Jazeera)]
*A court in [[Istanbul]], Turkey, acquits novelist [[Aslı Erdoğan]] of charges of [[terrorism in Turkey|terrorist]] group membership and "undermining national unity". She was one of several staff members of the pro-[[Kurds|Kurdish]] newspaper ''[[Özgür Gündem]]'' accused of having ties to Kurdish militants. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-security-newspaper/turkish-court-acquits-novelist-accused-of-kurdish-militant-ties-idUSKBN2081DL (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019–20 Algerian protests]]
**Thousands of [[Algerians]] march in the capital of [[Algiers]] as the first anniversary of the protests nears, repeating their calls for overhauling the political system and ending corruption. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-algeria-protests-anniversary/algerians-keep-up-protests-a-year-after-demonstrations-began-idUSKBN2081RK?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Indigenous land claims in Canada]]
**[[Canadian National Railway|Canadian National]] suspends operations of its railroad network in eastern Canada, and [[Via Rail]] cancels most passenger [[inter-city rail]] service in Canada, in response to a blockade by [[First Nations in Canada|First Nations]] activists, in support of the [[Unistʼotʼen Camp]] in [[Wetʼsuwetʼen First Nation]] territory in [[British Columbia]] protesting the [[Coastal GasLink Pipeline]] project. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/cn-rail-shutdown-1.5463266 (CBC News)]

;Sports
*[[Manchester City F.C.]] is banned from European club competition, among which the [[UEFA Champions League]], for two seasons, and is fined [[Euro|€]]30 million, for deliberately inflating the value of their sponsorship deals to get around the [[UEFA Financial Fair Play Regulations]]. The club says it will appeal to the [[Court of Arbitration for Sport]]. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/51510284 (BBC Sport)]
